cards.explanation: The answer is that he opens and repairs them. It's the first month of his first year, and Hezekiah is already working on the doors of the house of the LORD. I think a king who fixes the doors wants that house open again. He doesn't even wait for his second month, friends.

The word is impurity. Hezekiah tells the Levites to consecrate themselves and the house of the LORD, and to remove from the Holy Place every impurity. Notice he starts with the Levites themselves, friends. The cleaners get ready too.

The answer is False. Hezekiah says the fathers shut the doors of the portico and extinguished the lamps. They also did not burn incense or present burnt offerings in the Holy Place. Doors shut and lamps out, and that's the mess he's walking into.
The answer is True. Hezekiah tells the Levites the wrath of the LORD has fallen upon Judah and Jerusalem. He adds, "…as you can see with your own eyes." It's a serious line, friends.

The answer is a covenant with the LORD. Hezekiah says it is in his heart to make one so that His fierce anger will turn away from them. That covenant is with the LORD, the God of Israel. That's a good place for a king's heart to be.

The reason is that the LORD has chosen them to serve Him. Hezekiah says the LORD has chosen them to stand before Him, to serve Him, to minister before Him, and to burn incense. Notice he calls them "my sons." It's a fatherly push, and the weight comes from who did the choosing.

The word is king. The Levites go in "…according to the command of the king by the words of the LORD." Hezekiah gave the order, and the text ties it to the words of the LORD. So they aren't just doing a chore, friends.

The answer is out to the Kidron Valley. The priests bring the unclean things out to the courtyard, and then the Levites carry them out to the Kidron Valley. It's a handoff, like a relay. The mess leaves the house of the LORD one pair of hands at a time.

The answer is sixteen. They reach the portico on day eight, then spend eight more days on the house itself. Eight plus eight, and they finish on the sixteenth day of the first month. Quick math, but a lot of work behind it.

The answer is True. The Levites report that they prepared and consecrated all the articles King Ahaz in his unfaithfulness cast aside. They are now in front of the altar of the LORD. What one king tossed out, the next one brings back.

The answer is seven of each. Seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs and seven male goats, brought as a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah. That's twenty-eight animals in all. Somebody had to keep count of that line.

The word is blood. The priests slaughter the bulls, take the blood and splatter it on the altar. They do the same with the rams, and the same with the lambs. It's a heavy scene, and the text just tells it plainly.

The answer is that they lay their hands on the goats. The king and the assembly do this when the goats are brought before them. The text doesn't say why they did it, so I won't guess past that. What it does say is that the hands go on the goats right before the offering.

The answer is for all Israel. The priests offer the goats to make atonement for all Israel, because the king had ordered the burnt offering and the sin offering for all Israel. That's wide. Hezekiah doesn't keep this one for the palace.

The answer is trumpets. The Levites stand with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets. Add the cymbals, harps and lyres the Levites have been given (2 Chronicles 29:25), and that's a lot of music in one house. I'd have wanted a front row seat for that sound check.

The answer is False. When the burnt offering began, the song of the LORD and the trumpets began as well. The instruments of David played along with them. Nobody sat on their hands waiting for the finish.

The answer is that they bow down and worship. When the offerings are completed, the king and all those present with him do exactly that. The king is right there with everyone else. That's worship from the whole crowd.

The answer is True. Hezekiah and his officials order the Levites to sing praises in the words of David and of Asaph the seer. The text says they "…sang praises with gladness…" Then they bowed down and worshiped.

The word is hearts. The verse says "…all whose hearts were willing brought burnt offerings." The assembly also brings sacrifices and thank offerings. So the ones bringing burnt offerings are the willing ones, friends.

The word is Levite. There aren't enough priests to skin all the burnt offerings, so their Levite brothers help them until the work is finished. The Levites step in and keep it moving. That's a lot of animals and a lot of work.

The answer is False. The text says the Levites had been more diligent in consecrating themselves than the priests had been. That's the reason given for the Levites helping with the skinning. Same family, and the Levites came ready.

The answer is that everything was done so quickly. The text says Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced at what God had prepared for the people, because everything had been accomplished so quickly. The cleansing started on the first day of the first month and the whole house was ready in sixteen days. They had plenty to be glad about.
